title: Decision models for the workflow: classifiers for the family, ready, next question and route, from journeys
request: Phase 4: decision models for the workflow's own decisions, not only the data-science ones; a point that does not beat the rule stays in shadow.
spec: dclab_core/workflow_labels.py (labels from a journey's truth), dclab_rnd/workflow_models.py (collect, relabel, train, gate), journeys_workflow_sealed.json (30 people, hash pinned), shadow and routing reading the workflow models.
plan: Freeze a new sealed set of journeys before training anything: every earlier sealed set was spent and had shaped the rules.
Play the dev and spent journeys with a ledger of their own, on the rules alone, and label each workflow decision from the journey's truth.
Train one classifier per point with the column points' code; judge each once on the sealed journeys by the column points' gate.

decisions.decision: The sealed set was written by an agent that read only the journeys' format, the kinds and their replicas.
decisions.why: A set written by someone who knows the rules tests the rules' author, not the rules.

decisions.decision: A label is the set of answers the journey accepts, and the rules and a model are both scored right inside it.
decisions.why: Taking DCLab's answer as the label whenever it was acceptable made the rules right by construction.

decisions.decision: The product's own rules (the question cap, a re-ask with the columns, a file of cases defining the outcome, a blocked route) are not labelled.
decisions.why: Labelling them wrong gave a model a margin for ignoring the product's limits.

decisions.decision: Twelve workflow points get no classifier, each with its reason.
decisions.why: The validator owns the moves, the person owns the map edits, and the agents' points need recorded sessions' outcomes.

change: workflow_labels (Truth, Label with accepted sets, canonical, QUESTIONS, QUESTION_LIMIT), the runner, capture.next_question (every askable field as options, a check under its own name, the cap and the label file in the state, nothing recorded while a question waits), shadow.answerable and both model folders, routing.passed reading DWM results, decision_models.train's limits.

findings.defect: The route classifier's dev margin came from routes the rules refused.
findings.scenario: When every approach was blocked by an unmet need the rules chose none, the label named the expected approach, and a one-option list gave the classifier the answer.
findings.cause: The label ignored that the refusal was the product's rule.
findings.fix: A route the rules refused is not labelled.

findings.defect: For three points the label was DCLab's own answer whenever that answer was acceptable.
findings.scenario: 1334 of 1366 next-question labels equalled the rules' answer; a model giving another acceptable answer was graded wrong.
findings.cause: The label picked the rules' value out of the acceptable ones.
findings.fix: Labels became accepted sets, the learned value the first accepted in a fixed order, and both answerers are scored by membership (canonical).

findings.defect: A family the person stated counted as the rules' answer.
findings.scenario: 44 of 280 family rows were the person's own family.
findings.cause: capture records the stated family as the decision.
findings.fix: Rows used by a person are left out of the family set and counted in the manifest.

findings.defect: A sealed journey that failed to play shrank the gate's count without failing it.
findings.scenario: verdict was called without the expected count.
findings.cause: Failed plays were recorded, not judged.
findings.fix: A failed sealed play fails every point.

findings.defect: A crash after the sealed set was opened left it unspent.
findings.scenario: Only result files marked the set read.
findings.fix: A read marker is written before the sealed set is opened; every verdict is computed before any result is written.

findings.defect: Two sets reuse journey ids, so two people shared a group.
findings.scenario: JS-01 to JS-10 exist in the first sealed set and in the programme's.
findings.cause: The group was the id alone.
findings.fix: A person is the set and the id.

findings.defect: Programme journeys were played outside an empty routing scope.
findings.scenario: A workspace routing a model would have shaped the rules' baseline.
findings.cause: Only the standard journeys set the scope.
findings.fix: Every play runs in an empty scope with shadows off.

findings.defect: Contradiction checks were recorded under their own names, outside the options.
findings.scenario: labels_check and target_check would be graded wrong for a model that cannot answer them.
findings.cause: The recorded field was the raw one.
findings.fix: The capture records a check under its field.

findings.defect: The labels overruled Home's five-question cap and its re-ask of a known outcome.
findings.scenario: Every one of the rules' 34 misses was a stop at the cap or that re-ask: the whole margin.
findings.cause: The state did not say the cap was reached.
findings.fix: The state records steps_left; the cap and the re-ask are not labelled.

findings.defect: Once the card was settled the learned answer was a further question, never to stop.
findings.scenario: A promoted model would ask for the data plan on every turn.
findings.cause: The first accepted answer was a further field.
findings.fix: Once settled, stopping is the learned answer.

findings.defect: The training rows came from plays made before the fixes.
findings.scenario: The gate would play with other code than training.
findings.cause: raw.jsonl was rebuilt from the first collection.
findings.fix: Collected again with the fixed code.

findings.defect: A file of cases defines the outcome, yet the state counted the outcome as open.
findings.scenario: 18 rules' misses were stops while the outcome question had been withdrawn by the product.
findings.cause: The state lacked the label situation.
findings.fix: The state records labels=file and the outcome is then not open.

findings.defect: The next question's options listed five fields while Home asks ten.
findings.scenario: 138 labels fell outside the options a classifier renormalises over.
findings.cause: The capture's options were the plan's first five.
findings.fix: Every askable field is an option (QUESTIONS).

outcome: Four workflow points have cards beside the rules' score, the other twelve say why they have none; the sealed journeys are judged once by the column points' gate.
lessons: A label must never be chosen by the answer it judges; take the set of acceptable answers and score everyone inside it.
When the rules look wrong on a labelled set, look first for the product's own rule the labels ignore.
risks: Journeys are written people: dev measures these conversations, not real sessions.
